book_meta.work: short stories by Guy de Maupassant and Anton Chekhov
book_meta.author: Maupassant (d. 1893) and Chekhov (d. 1904)
book_meta.status: public domain — retold from the plots, not from any translation

sentences.ar: ولد وأبوه واقفين بالشارع من الصبح.
sentences.en: A boy and his father stood in the street since morning.

sentences.ar: أبوه كان بده يمد إيده ويشحد وما بيقدر.
sentences.en: His father wanted to put out his hand and beg and could not.

sentences.ar: الولد كان جعان لدرجة إنه شاف الدنيا بتلف.
sentences.en: The boy was so hungry the world seemed to spin.

sentences.ar: قرا كلمة على لافتة مطعم: محار.
sentences.en: He read a word on a restaurant sign: oysters.
He asked his father: what does oysters mean?

sentences.ar: قال أبوه: حيوان بحري، بياكلوه وهو حي.
sentences.en: His father said: a sea creature, they eat it alive.
The boy began imagining it and felt sick.

sentences.ar: وبنفس الوقت، صار يصرخ: بدي محار!
sentences.en: And at the same time, he began shouting: I want oysters!
Two men laughed at him and fed him.

sentences.ar: وأبوه ضل واقف جنبه وما مد إيده.
sentences.en: And his father stood beside him and did not put out his hand.
